claims.text: The initial material is an FCC/B2 eutectic HEA containing a homogeneous distribution of ordered B2 precipitates in an FCC matrix.
The initial FCC/B2 alloy exhibits high ductility.
Intermediate thermal aging promotes growth and ordering of coherent B2 precipitates without grain coarsening or impurity segregation.
Coherent ordered B2 precipitates cause transient brittleness by generating high lattice friction and impeding dislocation cross-slip.
Higher-temperature aging changes B2 precipitates from coherent platelets to semi-coherent or incoherent particles.
Loss of precipitate coherency reduces lattice friction.
The morphological and coherency transition allows Orowan looping or other dislocation-bypass mechanisms to dominate.
Evolution of local chemical order within B2 precipitates produces a change in FCC/B2 phase-boundary coherency.
Lattice mismatch and ordered domains hinder partial-dislocation motion through a friction effect.
Molecular-dynamics simulations of CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires found that friction associated with constituent-atom lattice-parameter differences hindered partial-dislocation motion.
Ductility varies non-monotonically with aging, falling sharply to near zero and then recovering at higher temperature or further precipitate evolution.
A critical B2 precipitate size and coherency maximize lattice friction and produce the ductility minimum.
Simple grain coarsening or impurity-segregation embrittlement would predict monotonic ductility loss or no transient recovery.
The embrittlement regime is limited to conditions where B2 precipitates are coherent and sufficiently ordered to impede dislocations but are not yet large enough for bypassing.
The temperature window for brittleness depends on constituent-element diffusion coefficients in B2.
The brittle transition should coincide with increased lattice friction or dislocation pinning inside B2.
Ductility recovery should correlate with loss of B2 precipitate coherency and associated morphology change.
A grain-size- and boundary-density-matched control without B2 should not exhibit the same brittle transition if the mechanism is B2-specific.

contradictions.description: The initial state already contains a homogeneous distribution of ordered B2 precipitates, whereas the hypothesis attributes the brittle state to aging-induced formation of coherent ordered B2 precipitates. It is not clarified whether aging forms new precipitates or only changes the size, degree of order, or coherency of pre-existing B2.
